verses.text: On a Sabbath—the second one after the first—Jesus was walking through grain fields. His disciples picked heads of grain, rubbed them in their hands, and ate.
Some Pharisees said, “Why are you doing something the Law doesn’t allow on the Sabbath?”
Jesus answered, “Haven’t you read what David did when he and the people with him were hungry?”
“He went into God’s house, took the bread of the Presence, ate it, and shared it with his companions—even though only priests were allowed to eat it.”
Then he told them, “The Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.”
On another Sabbath, Jesus went into the synagogue and taught. A man was there whose right hand was shriveled.
The legal teachers and Pharisees watched Jesus closely, waiting to see if he’d heal on the Sabbath so they could accuse him.
Jesus knew what they were thinking. He told the man with the shriveled hand, “Get up and stand here in the middle.” The man got up and stood there.
Then Jesus said to them, “Here’s a question for you: on the Sabbath, is it right to do good or harm? To save a life or destroy one?”
He looked around at everyone and said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” The man did, and his hand was restored, healthy like the other one.
The Pharisees were furious. They started discussing what they could do to Jesus.
Around that time, Jesus went up the mountain to pray. He spent the whole night praying to God. 🙏
When morning came, he called his disciples and chose twelve of them, whom he also named apostles:
Simon, whom he named Peter; Andrew his brother; James; John; Philip; Bartholomew;
Matthew; Thomas; James son of Alphaeus; Simon, who was called the Zealot;
Judas son of James; and Judas Iscariot, who became a traitor.

Jesus came down the mountain with them and stood on a level place. A crowd of his disciples and a huge number of people from Judea, Jerusalem, and the coastal regions of Tyre and Sidon were there. They came to hear him and be healed.
People troubled by unclean spirits came too, and they were healed.
The whole crowd tried to touch Jesus, because power came from him and healed them all.
Jesus looked at his disciples and said, “You who are poor are blessed, because God’s Kingdom belongs to you.”
“You who are hungry now are blessed, because you’ll be satisfied. You who are weeping now are blessed, because you’ll laugh.”
“You’re blessed when people hate you, push you out, mock you, and call your name evil because of the Son of Man.”
“When that day comes, celebrate and leap for joy! Your reward in heaven is great. Their ancestors treated the prophets the same way. 🙌”
“But trouble is coming for you who are rich—you’ve already received your comfort.”
“Trouble for you who are full now—you’ll be hungry. Trouble for you who laugh now—you’ll mourn and weep.”
“Trouble when everyone speaks well of you. Their ancestors did the same for the false prophets.”
“But to all of you listening, I say: love your enemies. Do good to those who hate you.”
“Bless those who curse you, and pray for those who mistreat you.”
“If someone strikes you on one cheek, offer the other too. If someone takes your coat, don’t hold back your shirt either.”
“Give to everyone who asks you. If someone takes what belongs to you, don’t demand it back.”
“Treat people exactly as you want them to treat you.”
“If you love only the people who love you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners love the people who love them.”
“If you do good only to people who do good to you, what credit is that? Sinners do that too.”
“If you lend only to people you expect to repay you, what credit is that? Even sinners lend to sinners to get the same amount back.”
“Instead, love your enemies, do good, and lend without expecting repayment. Your reward will be great, and you’ll be children of the Most High. God is kind even to the ungrateful and evil.”
“Be merciful, then, just as your Father is merciful.”
“Don’t judge, and you won’t be judged. Don’t condemn, and you won’t be condemned. Forgive, and you’ll be forgiven.”
“Give, and it’ll be given to you: a good measure, packed down, shaken together, and spilling over. The measure you use will be used for you too.”
Jesus told them a parable: “Can a blind person lead another blind person? Won’t they both fall into a ditch?”
“A student isn’t above their teacher. But when fully trained, each student will be like their teacher.”
“Why do you notice the tiny speck in your brother’s eye but miss the plank in your own?”

“How can you say, ‘Brother, let me get that speck out of your eye,’ when you can’t see the plank in your own? You hypocrite! First get the plank out of your eye. Then you’ll see clearly enough to remove the speck from your brother’s eye.”
“A good tree doesn’t produce rotten fruit, and a rotten tree doesn’t produce good fruit.”
“You can tell what kind of tree it is by its fruit. People don’t pick figs from thornbushes or grapes from brambles.”
“A good person brings good things out of the good stored in their heart. An evil person brings evil things out of the evil stored there. What fills the heart spills out of the mouth.”
“Why call me ‘Lord, Lord,’ and then ignore what I say?”
“I’ll show you what someone is like who comes to me, hears my words, and acts on them.”
“They’re like someone building a house who dug deep and laid the foundation on rock. When floodwater surged against that house, it couldn’t shake it, because it was built on rock.”

“But whoever hears my words and doesn’t act on them is like someone who built a house on bare ground without a foundation. The flood smashed into it, and it collapsed right away. That house was completely wrecked.”
